subject: Post-demo: access evidence runbook + sample delivery
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: access evidence runbook + sample delivery

Hi Lydia — thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the access/evidence deliverable we discussed: 

Summary of ask from CareCore: a reproducible "who/what/when" extract for production access events covering user-level and service-account access, suitable for audit review and ingestion into your ticketing/GRC systems. Key constraints you mentioned: PII minimization, per-tenant retention policy, timezone normalization, and CSV deliverable with hashing/redaction options.

Proposed next steps from Redwood: 
- We’ll provide a short runbook that describes the export process, schema, and retention options (CSV gzipped, UTC times, ISO8601).
- Provide a redacted sample CSV (single-day snapshot) with a mapping doc showing which fields contain hashed values vs plain text.
- Security will outline recommended hashing/salting approach and available redaction options.
- Timeline: sample + runbook within 48 business hours, full export options & SLA terms in the following week.

Attaching: runbook stub and a suggested CSV schema (see attachments).

Action items: 
1) Lydia: confirm the columns you need in the sample (or tell us any additional fields required for your SIEM/GRC ingest).
2) CareCore: confirm any legal/retention minima (e.g., 90/365/730 days) so we can propose a configuration.
3) Redwood (Marissa/Ben): will prepare sample and technical notes.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if you'd like us to walk through the sample.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@carecore.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit.patel@careprocure.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: access evidence runbook + sample delivery

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before you produce the sample: 

1) Required columns: care team will need the following columns at minimum for our SIEM ingest — timestamp, actor_identifier, actor_email, actor_role, resource_path, action, session_id, request_id, and IP address. If you have token_type or client_id we can map those too.

2) Timezone: please normalize timestamps to UTC (ISO8601 with millisecond precision).

3) PII & hashing: we cannot receive raw email addresses unless they are pseudonymized. Would you provide emails hashed with SHA-256 + per-customer salt, and a separate mapping file (stored separately under our legal/secure share) if required for forensics? We also need to understand what level of reversibility Redwood supports.

4) Retention: our default is 365 days, but procurement (Amit) may negotiate 90 or 730 depending on contract. Please include the export retention cutoff in the runbook (how to request longer historical extracts).

5) Format: CSV is fine. A sample 1-day snapshot (<=10k rows) is preferred. Please include a header row with clear column names we can map.

6) Evidence authenticity: we need a short statement about immutability guarantees and whether exported rows include a monotonic sequence or event_id we can use to detect tampering.

If possible, deliver the sample and runbook by EOD Wednesday (48h). We'll schedule a quick 30-min sync after we review.

Thanks,
Lydia Chen
Security & Compliance Lead — CareCore Health
lydia.chen@carecore.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: access evidence runbook + sample delivery

Hi Lydia — Ben from Security here. Appreciate the specificity — below is the proposed export schema and PII handling approach we will include in the runbook. Let me know if anything should be added.

Proposed CSV schema (columns):
- event_time_utc (ISO8601 with ms)
- event_id (opaque monotonic id assigned at write)
- actor_id (internal user id, e.g., SAML nameid or service account id)
- actor_email_hash (SHA256 hex, per-customer salt included only in our KMS-held config; we can provide a separate mapping under legal request)
- actor_role (string: admin/developer/service)
- resource_type (string)
- resource_path (string)
- action (read/write/delete/login/token_refresh)
- session_id (string)
- request_id (trace id)
- source_ip (IP address)
- client_id (optional, OAuth client id)
- token_type (optional)
- retention_cutoff (ISO8601)
- evidence_tag (for correlation with runbook)

PII handling recommendations:
- We will hash actor_email using SHA-256 with a per-customer salt generated and stored in our KMS. Hash output provided in hex. This is irreversible without access to the salt + KMS key.
- If you require reversible mapping for select requests, we can provide an escrowed mapping export under a separate legal process (documented in the runbook).
- Optionally include a redacted actor_email_first_last (first 1 / last 1 characters) for quick triage — still not reversible.

Timestamping / timezone:
- All timestamps in the export will be normalized to UTC and formatted as 2027-05-30T21:03:12.123Z.
- event_id is monotonic per-shard and suitable for tamper detection; we will include a signed manifest file (HMAC-SHA256) over the gzipped CSV for integrity verification.

Retention & exports: 
- Default retention configuration we can apply per-customer: 90 / 365 / 730 days.
- For historical extracts beyond the retention window we can run a bounded export (charges apply).

Delivery format & timeline: 
- Deliverable: gzipped CSV (utf-8) + signed manifest + runbook markdown.
- Sample: we can produce the 1-day sample and runbook within 48 business hours.
- Full export SLA: propose 5 business days for a full tenant export up to 90 days, longer windows negotiated in contract.

Attachments included with my email: sample_who_when_utc_20270529.csv_stub (single-day sample), access_evidence_schema_v1.csv_stub, runbook_access-evidence.md_stub.

If this looks good Jordan, we’ll prepare the sample and deliver to the Drive link (secured) you provided; otherwise tell us any changes and we’ll adjust.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Security Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Ben — that schema looks to cover our needs. Two quick asks before you finalize: 

1) For the signed manifest, can you include the HMAC key id and the algorithm in the runbook so our ingest can validate automatically?
2) For the per-customer salt: confirm that Redwood will not include the salt in the same Drive share as the sample. We prefer a separate secure channel.

We accept the 48-hour sample timeline. Please drop the sample CSV and runbook in the shared CareCore folder (we gave you access: https://drive.carecore.com/s/secure-evidence) and notify us once uploaded. After review, let's do a 30-minute call Thursday to confirm mapping to our SIEM and any procurement questions (Amit is cc'ed for timing/contract).

Best,
Lydia
